notes: Exercised indirectly by deep-code-review's eval 1 (as a dispatched subagent). This file covers the standalone human-facing path, which gets less exercise and has had less design attention. Ground truth: ../../deep-code-review/meta/ground-truth/ninniku-cel-alert.md

evals.name: standalone-logic-hunt
evals.prompt: Something feels off about the alert evaluation code I just wrote but I can't put my finger on it. Can you dig into the logic and tell me what edge cases I've missed?
evals.expected_output: Markdown (not JSON — this is the human path): a behavior model, findings each carrying an execution trace with concrete inputs, a questions-I-couldn't-answer section, and a proposed memory diff awaiting approval.

assertions.text: Reports at least one silent fallback that inverts a decision (angle A4)
Reports the DeleteAlert lifecycle gap (angle A1)
Reports the expression injection via unvalidated string interpolation (angle A7)
Every finding carries an execution trace naming concrete inputs and the resulting wrong output
Output is markdown, not a JSON block — the standalone path was detected correctly
States which angles ran and which were gated out
Includes a 'questions I couldn't answer from the code' section with at least one real intent question
Proposes a memory diff and waits for approval rather than writing it
Does not write anything to the ninniku working tree or .claude/ directory
No finding rests solely on inferred intent — those appear as questions instead
